pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered with the prospect taking notes at the rep's request ('do you have something to write, like pen and paper?' — 'I will open the notebook'), covering 3-4 sessions of 30-40 minutes, tailored programming, 5-10 minutes of daily mobility for hips and back, and the teach-you-to-fish framing. Asked whether it would work for him he said 'Yes, it's great for me.' The one moment of independent reaction was a mild disagreement with the rep's framing — told that hitting 30 minutes would be difficult at first, he replied 'No, 30 minutes is very simple for me. And it's free for me. No problem from 30 to 40 minutes.'

The pillar most relevant to him, since he had already identified nutrition as his weakest area — 'Maybe I'm not organized regarding nutrition... this point is critical to my target.' Presented as what/when/how much, clean food, no tracking or weighing, a weekly pizza, and explicitly localised — 'Trevor will prepare this nutrition plan around your schedule and around your lifestyle. So what products are available to you in your shop, in your market.' Response: 'Yes, it makes sense. Great for me and a great explanation.'

Presented as weekly check-ins in one app plus the ability to flag a hard week in advance, with the negotiating-with-yourself frame: 'before, when you don't have a coach it's easy to fall off because you're negotiating only with yourself, but now when you want to skip a day you will have to tell it to Trevor.' Response: 'No, more effective. Thank you for your great explanation.' Note that all three pillar reactions are short, uniform and appreciative in the same register, which across a language barrier is weak evidence of engagement — none of the three drew a question, a challenge or a personal application, unlike every other sales call in this batch.

anchors.raw: I bought some kettlebells at the home, and some cordbells, and some other tools, such as dumbbells, to handle my time to make a gym at my home... I was 94 kilograms, I was 94, but through my workouts on kettlebells, I lose some kilograms
anchors.note: He has already built the home gym and already lost 6-8 kg with it, unsupervised. What he is paying $6,000 for is programming, nutrition structure and accountability on top of equipment and results he produced himself. The rep acknowledged the training half of this ('you've already started your kettlebell workouts') but never addressed the self-directed result, which is the strongest argument the prospect had against needing to pay.

unmet_demand.want: Visible results by a fixed date — the wedding on 15 October, roughly four months after this call
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is sold in six and twelve month terms and the rep recommended six months, which runs two months past the event. He raised the mismatch himself at 00:02:17 — 'So we don't have a lot of time' — and again at 00:29:31, and never resolved it. There is no four-month structure and no stated position on what is achievable by October.

unmet_demand.want: To settle payment after the session rather than on the call
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Raised at 00:32:49 and unresolved on the recording, which ends nine seconds later. Whether the process can accommodate it is not knowable from this file.

unmet_demand.want: The sale conducted at a pace and in language he could reliably follow
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not a product gap but a delivery one, and it belongs here because it determines whether anything else was actually received. He asked for repetition at 00:08:32, 00:13:09, 00:16:00 and 00:28:31, and the pace, idiom and vocabulary were unchanged throughout. Nothing in the process provides for a comprehension check before commitment.
